_README: Availability of the protected (indoor / covered) network, by hour and weekday.
An arcade at 21:00 is not expensive, it is SHUT. That is a hard gate, not a cost, and
it is the one property of the indoor network that does not belong in the thermal
model at all -- server/hours.py applies it by removing edges from the graph, before
THESE HOURS ARE EDITORIAL ESTIMATES, NOT DATA. OpenStreetMap carries opening_hours on
2 of the 1232 walkable indoor ways in this extract, so there is nothing to import.
Every entry below is a plausible default chosen to make the gate behave sensibly, and
none has been checked against a published trading-hours page. verified=false says so
on every class; anything that ships as a claim about a real building has to be
checked first. The MECHANISM is correct; the COVERAGE is a data problem.
Hours are local (Australia/Melbourne), [open, close) in decimal hours. null = shut all
day. A class with "always": true is never gated.
